canonical_statement: A real standard Wiener process on nonnegative time, specified by its centered Gaussian independent-increment finite-dimensional laws and almost-sure initial value zero, has a coordinatewise modification whose paths are almost surely both continuous and nowhere differentiable on the nonnegative-time domain.
domain_and_universes: Omega : Type u with MeasurableSpace; P : Measure Omega with IsProbabilityMeasure; X,Y : Real -> Omega -> Real; target is Prop in universe u
hypotheses: on every increasing nonnegative finite grid, adjacent increments are mutually independent
each adjacent increment has gaussianReal 0 with variance equal to its time length
conclusion: There exists a coordinatewise modification Y of X and one P-almost-everywhere event on which the path t |-> Y t omega is ContinuousOn Ici 0 and is not DifferentiableWithinAt at every point of Ici 0.

representation_decisions.wiener_law: finite ordered nonnegative grids, iIndepFun adjacent increments, and exact centered gaussianReal increment laws
representation_decisions.endpoint: DifferentiableWithinAt on Set.Ici 0, hence domain-relative at zero
representation_decisions.event: continuity and nowhere differentiability share one full-measure event

degenerate_cases: The zero-length increment is allowed and has gaussianReal 0 0. Finite grids may repeat times. The n = 0 grid is allowed. The endpoint t = 0 uses the domain-relative derivative. No negative-time claim is made.

killed: broadened the conclusion to all real time
